# Tutorials

The tutorials teach Starsim through one example: a simplified measles outbreak in a town, which gains a latent period, age groups, vaccination, other towns, data to fit it to, and more. Each takes 10 to 20 minutes, starts with the model so far (so you can start at any one), and ends with exercises. The [user guide](user_guide.qmd) covers each topic in full.

## Core tutorials

The core tutorials build models of compartments: groups of people, by state and by age or place. Starsim runs them as equations, as stochastic models, or as agents.

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-6}
[**T1 – Getting started**](tutorials/t1_intro.qmd)

A measles outbreak as an SIR model: run it, plot it, and check what Starsim built.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T2 – Building a model**](tutorials/t2_model.qmd)

The first model in more depth: states, transitions, parameters, time, and results.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T3 – Building a disease**](tutorials/t3_disease.qmd)

A latent period, how long people stay in each state, waning immunity, and deaths, with the diagram and equations.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T4 – Age groups and contacts**](tutorials/t4_ages.qmd)

Who mixes with whom: age groups, contact matrices, and real populations.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T5 – Interventions and scenarios**](tutorials/t5_interventions.qmd)

Vaccination, school terms, and comparing scenarios across many runs.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T6 – Geography and mixing**](tutorials/t6_places.qmd)

Several towns, and how an outbreak travels between them.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T7 – Data and calibration**](tutorials/t7_calibration.qmd)

Fitting the model to reported cases, and projecting from the fit.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T8 – Stratification and co-transmission**](tutorials/t8_strata.qmd)

Splitting a model by more than age, and two diseases that affect each other.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T9 – Custom modules**](tutorials/t9_modules.qmd)

Writing your own behavior as code, while keeping the model compartmental.
:::

:::

## Agent-based modeling

These tutorials are for models that need individual people: contact networks, individual histories, births and deaths, and interventions that target individuals.

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-6}
[**A1 – Diseases**](tutorials/a1_diseases.qmd)

A disease as agents: individual states, histories, and differences between people.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**A2 – Networks**](tutorials/a2_networks.qmd)

Who meets whom, one contact at a time: random, sexual, and other networks.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**A3 – Demographics**](tutorials/a3_demographics.qmd)

Births, deaths, and pregnancy for individual people.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**A4 – Interventions**](tutorials/a4_interventions.qmd)

Interventions that target individuals: eligibility, testing, and treatment.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**A5 – Custom modules**](tutorials/a5_modules.qmd)

Writing agent-level logic of your own, from a small change to a new module.
:::

:::

The answers to the exercises are in the [solutions](tutorials/solutions.qmd).

::: {.callout-tip}
## Running tutorials locally

Each tutorial can be downloaded as a Jupyter notebook: look for the download button at the top of the page. Or, to run them all locally: clone the Starsim repository, install Starsim (`pip install -e .`), go to `docs/tutorials`, and open them in Jupyter (`jupyter lab`, with `jupytext` installed to open `.qmd` files directly, or run `./convert_notebooks` first).
:::
